title: Kenyan Lamb Stew
community: Popular across Kenya — especially for celebrations and Eid
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Lamb Stew — tender bone-in lamb pieces slowly simmered in a fragrant tomato, onion, and garlic sauce with warming spices until the meat is falling off the bone. Richer and more aromatic than beef stew, lamb stew is Kenya's celebratory meat at its most comforting.
longDesc: Lamb is particularly associated with celebration in Kenyan culture — served at Eid, weddings, and family feasts. Its natural richness and distinctive aroma pair beautifully with the Kenyan spice base, and its slightly shorter cooking time than goat makes it more practical for everyday cooking while still delivering a depth of flavour that beef cannot match.
steps: Brown seasoned lamb in hot oil in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Return lamb. Add stock, potatoes, and carrots.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 60—70 minutes until the lamb is completely tender.
Season, garnish with coriander, and serve.
chefTips: Lamb is fattier than goat — skim excess fat from the surface during cooking if preferred.
Lamb shoulder is the ideal cut — enough fat to stay moist, enough connective tissue to add body.
commonMistakes: Using lean leg meat — it can dry out during long simmering.
Not browning the meat — the stew lacks depth.

faqs.q: What is the difference between lamb stew and goat stew?
faqs.a: Lamb has a milder, slightly sweeter flavour and more fat than goat. Goat is leaner with a more intense, complex flavour. Both make excellent stews — the choice depends on personal preference and availability.

cookingScience: Lamb shoulder has a higher fat content than goat, which bastes the meat during cooking and keeps it moist. The collagen in the shoulder converts to gelatin during simmering, enriching the sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Lamb shoulder is a less popular cut that benefits from slow cooking — buying it supports nose-to-tail eating.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze for up to 3 months.
reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Rich in complete protein, iron, and zinc.
Good source of B12 and selenium.
Higher in healthy omega-3 fatty acids than beef.
culturalNote: Lamb stew is a celebration dish in Kenya — particularly associated with Eid al-Adha when lamb is slaughtered and shared with family, neighbours, and those in need. The aroma of lamb stew simmering is the smell of generosity and community.
regionalVariations: Spiced lamb with extra garam masala.
